jobs.description:
Tulsa Optics Tutor

BuffTutor is a network of experienced and passionate tutors who provide academic assistance to college & high school students. We are always hiring dedicated tutors; if you love teaching, join us!

Responsibilities:
• Provide 1-on-1 in-person or online tutoring to university and/or high school students. We are primarily hiring STEM tutors to assist with courses such as Math, Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics etc.

BENEFITS:
• Set your own rate.
• In-person & online tutoring available; meet wherever works for you.
• Set your own schedule; meet whenever works for you.
• Work with as many (or as few) students as you would like to.

QUALIFICATIONS:
• Have at least a 3.0 or better major GPA (out of 4.0).
• Have earned a B or better in the courses you wish to tutor.
• Have at least one year (or two semesters) of experience as a tutor, teacher, teaching/learning assistant or instructor.
• Have excellent communication skills and you must be fluent in the language that you teach in. Foreign Language tutors must be fluent in the Foreign Language they wish to tutor.

ABOUT BUFFTUTOR:

BuffTutor is dedicated to connecting students with intelligent and experienced tutors. We primarily focus on university level tutoring, but also work with high school and middle school students. More than just another tutor list, we prioritize the academic needs of our students while also treating our tutors with dignity and respect:
• We have some of the strictest eligibility criteria and challenging proficiency exams. Only the best can join our network!
• Tutors can set their own schedule. Our motto is quality is more important than quantity. Take on one student but be the best tutor for that student!
• Tutors can set their own rate. Earn what you are worth!
• We review student evaluations to help us keep the best tutor in our network.

BuffTutor was founded in 2009 and since then we have helped thousands of students and parents connect with affordable and passionate educators!

Please note that tutors are independent contractors, not employees. All applicants must already have work permissions; applicants who are students must be able to work an off-campus position. We do not sponsor individuals and we cannot work with F-1 or J-1 international students

jobs.title: Metrology Specialist | CMM Programming, GD&T & Precision Inspection
jobs.description:
25th September, 2026

Own the CMM programs and inspection plans behind high-volume die-cast parts, on-site in Sallisaw, OK.
Metrology Specialist | CMM Programming, GD&T & Precision Inspection

Some metrology roles mean running someone else's program on repeat. This one puts you in charge of the measurement side. You'd write and maintain the CMM programs, inspection plans and procedures that decide whether complex die-cast components meet their dimensional, geometric and tolerance requirements.

You would be the person the Quality team relies on when a dimension is in question. Your analysis against engineering drawings, GD&T and customer specifications directly shapes defect reduction and process optimization in a high-volume production environment.

If you like precision work but also want to be close to the process, this role offers both. Your time is split between a climate-controlled quality lab and the active plant floor.
Why This Opportunity Is Different

This role goes beyond inspection into real influence on the process. You would partner directly with Quality, Engineering and Production to troubleshoot dimensional anomalies and support root-cause investigations. You would also work with tooling and process engineers on die-casting process improvements and measurement efficiency.

The breadth of exposure is strong too: CMM programming across multiple platforms, First Article Inspections, PPAP submissions, quality system audits, and calibration with traceability to national standards, all within ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 frameworks. For a metrology professional who wants to grow skills that are recognized across manufacturing, this is a strong platform.
What You'll Be Doing
• Verify that die-cast components conform to dimensional, geometric and tolerance requirements using CMM, calipers, micrometers, height gauges and optical measurement systems
• Program and operate CMMs such as Zeiss, Mitutoyo and Hexagon to measure complex geometries and critical dimensions
• Create, maintain and execute measurement programs, inspection plans and standard procedures
• Analyze measurement data to confirm full compliance with engineering drawings, GD&T standards and customer specifications
• Partner with Quality, Engineering and Production to resolve dimensional anomalies and support root-cause investigations
• Support First Article Inspections, PPAP submissions and quality system audits
• Calibrate and maintain metrology tools so measurements stay traceable to national standards
• Keep accurate inspection records in line with ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 requirements
• Work with tooling and process engineers to improve die-casting processes and measurement efficiency
What We're Looking For
• High School Diploma or GED required
• 3+ years of quality inspection or metrology experience in a manufacturing environment
• Proven proficiency operating and programming CMM software platforms
• Strong expertise in GD&T
• Hands-on mastery of precision measuring instruments and blueprint interpretation
• Familiarity with ISO 9001 or IATF 16949 quality management frameworks
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and metrology or data management software
• Associate Degree or technical certification in Metrology, Engineering Technology or a related field is preferred
• Die-casting process and tooling experience, SPC and data analysis tools, and practical QMS knowledge are strong assets
• A detail-oriented, collaborative professional who can explain measurement findings clearly to engineering and production teams
Compensation & Work Model
• Compensation is competitive and will be discussed during the screening process.
• Full-time, on-site.
Location & Travel
• On-site in Sallisaw, Oklahoma
• Work is split between a climate-controlled quality laboratory and an active manufacturing plant floor
• Requires standing for extended periods and working around noise, heat and active machinery
• Must be able to occasionally lift up to 25 lbs
About TAPP Workforce Solutions

Overview

In this role you will develop and apply advanced simulation and AI-driven techniques to enable virtual calibration and reduce physical testing. You will work at the intersection of controls engineering, digital transformation, and customer-focused delivery to advance automotive virtual engineering. You will build high-fidelity, real-time capable models and drive adoption of simulation tools across teams. This position offers impact by shaping calibration workflows, cloud-based scalability, and integration of AI with model-based approaches. You will collaborate cross-functionally to deliver value to customers and accelerate EV calibration programs.

• Collaborate with propulsion controls and calibration teams; maintain requirements and feedback channels; track KPIs; guide model usage and ensure pre-delivery compatibility with customer systems.
• Integrate AI with model-based approaches; implement RAG systems; design cloud setups for scalable virtual calibration; correlate models with physical data; drive virtual calibration initiatives for EVs; explore emerging virtual engineering technologies.
Key requirements
• Background in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred
• 3+ years in automotive controls engineering, simulation, or related field
• Proficiency in Simulink, GT-Power, Amesim, MATLAB, Python, C/C++, and scripting languages
• Experience with vehicle calibration processes and methodologies (INCA, Vector tools, or similar)
• Knowledge of AI/ML technologies, Neural Networks, LLMs, and cloud computing (AWS, Azure)

• Strong problem-solving, analytical skills, and systems thinking; collaborative with cross-functional teams

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Physics
jobs.description:
WAKE FOREST UNIVERSITY. The Department of Physics invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Physics that will start July 1, 2027.


Qualifications: A Ph.D. in Physics or a closely related field is required for the position. Qualified applicants will demonstrate their ability to teach physics courses, initiate and sustain original research and scholarship in biophysics and/or materials science, and contribute to an academic environment that fosters learning and growth for all its stakeholders. We are particularly interested in candidates conducting experimental research in biophotonics, biomaterials, or bioelectronics and in candidates pursuing AI-focused research in biophysics or materials science using computational and/or experimental approaches. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to benefit from extensive facilities including new state-of-the-art equipment obtained through recent university investments. Ideally, the successful candidate will work at the intersection between materials science and biophysics and will strengthen the connections between those groups.


Position Summary: This individual will be expected to teach physics courses at the graduate and undergraduate level, engage in scholarly activities, participate in departmental, College, and University service, and contribute to the University’s community outreach efforts. In keeping with the Teacher-Scholar model practiced at Wake Forest University, the successful candidate will establish a vigorous, externally supported research program and create a learning environment that welcomes all students into scientific study and supports their ongoing success. Candidates whose research interests complement those of current Wake Forest Physics faculty are particularly encouraged to apply, as we seek to increase opportunities for collaborative research.


About the Department of Physics: The department offers BA, BS, MS, and PhD degrees in Physics, an MS and certificate in Quantum Information Sciences, and a BS in Biophysics. The department emphasizes interdisciplinary study and close student-faculty collaboration. Opportunities for multidisciplinary collaboration include the Center for Functional Materials, the Nano and Quantum Technologies Laboratory, the Translational Science Center, the Center for Molecular Signaling, and the other centers at the university, as well as collaborations with faculty at the Wake Forest University School of Medicine. Additional information about the department is available at physics.wfu.edu.


About Wake Forest University: Founded in 1834, Wake Forest University is a private, coeducational institution dedicated to academic excellence in liberal arts, graduate, and professional education. With more than 5,400 undergraduates and 3,800 graduate and professional students, Wake Forest is a collegiate university offering a vibrant, intellectual community with a rich cultural life, an impressive array of facilities, and a strong athletics program competing in the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC). Since its founding, the University has adopted the motto Pro Humanitate, which is exemplified by a deep institutional commitment to public service and engagement with the world.


Wake Forest University is located in Winston-Salem, a beautiful, mid-sized city in the Piedmont-Triad region of North Carolina.


Equal Opportunity Statement The University is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes all qualified candidates to apply without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, disability and military or veteran status.



Accommodations for Applicants. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please contact A​skHR@wfu.edu or (336) 758-4700.

jobs.description:
Description

Job Title: Scientific ProgrammerClearance Required: Public Trust Work Location: Remote

Alpha Omega is seeking a qualified Scientific Programmer in support of our NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) Data Stewardship Division (DSD) customer. This division works in partnership with NOAA and the broader community to develop and maintain a robust and efficient infrastructure of hardware, software, and processes to support the ingest, long-term preservation, and delivery of environmental data products spanning the depths of the ocean to the surface of the sun. In this role, this individual will be responsible for stewardship of our nation's environmental data.

Key Responsibilities:

Infrastructure Modernization: Drive the transition of legacy systems to modern architectures.

System Maintenance: Proactively monitor and maintain aging infrastructure to ensure high availability and performance.

Development & Integration: Design and implement scalable solutions using serverless technologies and robust backend scripting.

Documentation & Quality Control: Maintain rigorous documentation standards by utilizing Pull Requests (PRs) to record architectural changes, code updates, and completed tasks.

CI/CD Management: Oversee automated deployment pipelines to ensure code quality and streamlined delivery cycles.

Required Qualifications:

Experience/Skills:
• 2 years of experience.
• Programming & Scripting: Proficiency in Python and Bash for automation and data processing.
• Cloud Infrastructure: Hands-on experience with AWS Lambda and serverless architecture.
• Web Technologies: Strong understanding of React and TypeScript for front-end interface management.
• Database Management: Experience writing and optimizing PL/SQL queries and managing relational databases.
• Version Control & DevOps: Advanced knowledge of Git and GitLab CI/CD workflows.
• API Development: Experience building and consuming RESTful APIs.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience/Skills:
• Data Stewardship: Previous experience working within data-heavy contracts or meteorological data formats.
• Legacy Migration: Proven track record of successfully "lifting and shifting" or refactoring aging infrastructure into cloud-native environments.
• Agile Methodology: Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment with a focus on iterative delivery.
• System Security: Familiarity with implementing security best practices within AWS environments.

Education:
• BS/BA Degree in an IT/IS field, such as Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering or a related field, or equivalent bootcamp/self-taught experience.

Salary and Benefit Information:

The likely salary range for this position is $60,000 - $62,000. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. There are multiple factors that are considered in determining final pay for a position, including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, certifications and competencies that align to the specified role, education and certifications as well as contract provisions regarding labor categories that are specific to the position and could fall outside of this range.

Application Deadline: December 7, 2026

Joining the Alpha Omega team entitles you to participate in all retirement benefits, plans of deferred compensation, health and insurance benefits, and other such benefits as set forth in the company's policy and benefits manuals. See below, to name a few:
• 15 days PTO including paid parental, military, and bereavement leave
• Eleven (11) paid Federal holidays, five of which are floating holidays (as designated by the company's holiday schedule each year)
• Health and Dental Insurance (including 100% employer paid premiums for employee coverage under the HDHP health plan)
• Life Insurance, STD/LTD term disability coverage, with employer paid premiums
• 401 (k) plan with a match that is 100% vested after you complete two years of service
• FSA/DFSA/HSA flex
